steps.title: The grammar we start from
steps.explain: Simplifying removes everything the grammar does not need, in a fixed order: 1a non-generating variables, 1b unreachable symbols, 2 ε-productions, 3 unit productions, 4 useless symbols again. Each step works on the output of the step before it, never on the original.
lines: P: S → AB | b
P: A → aA | ε
P: B → bC | b
P: C → A
7 productions, 4 variables

steps.title: Step 1a · Variables that generate nothing
steps.explain: Work bottom-up: a variable is generating if one of its productions has only terminals and generating variables on the right. ε counts as a terminal string, so A → ε makes A generating.
lines: generating, round 1: S (S → b)   A (A → ε)   B (B → b)
generating, round 2: C (C → A)
generating, round 3: nothing new → stop
not generating: none, so all 4 variables survive

quiz.question: Step 1a: which variables can never produce a terminal string?
quiz.why: Every variable reaches a terminal string, so nothing is removed. The check still has to be written.

steps.title: Step 1b · Symbols unreachable from S
steps.explain: Work top-down from S: a symbol is reachable if it appears on the right of a production of a reachable variable. 1a must come first, because deleting a non-generating variable can cut the only path to another symbol.
lines: reachable, round 0: S
reachable, round 1: S → AB reaches A, B   S → b reaches b
reachable, round 2: A → aA reaches a   B → bC reaches C
unreachable from S: none

steps.title: Step 2 · Remove the ε-productions
steps.explain: Find the nullable variables (those that can derive ε). Then rewrite every production with each nullable symbol present or absent, in every combination except "all absent", and delete the ε-productions.
lines: nullable, round 1: A (A → ε)
nullable, round 2: C (C → A)
nullable = {A, C}   (not nullable: S, B)
S → AB gives S → AB | B
A → aA gives A → aA | a
A → ε is deleted
B → bC gives B → bC | b
C → A stays as it is: dropping its only symbol would create a new ε-production
the other 2 productions have no nullable symbol and stay unchanged
S is not nullable, so ε ∉ L(G): the language is unchanged
careful: this step CREATED the unit production S → B. Step 3 must re-read the whole grammar

quiz.question: Step 2: which variables are nullable?
quiz.why: A variable is nullable if it has A → ε, or a production whose right-hand side is made of nullable variables only. Follow the chains to the end.

steps.title: Step 3 · Remove the unit productions
steps.explain: Re-read the CURRENT grammar for productions A → B (step 2 may have created some). Follow every chain to its end: if A ⇒ … ⇒ B by unit productions, A receives all of B's non-unit productions.
lines: unit productions in the current grammar: S → B (created by step 2),  C → A
chain S ⇒ B: B's non-unit productions are bC | b  →  add S → bC
chain C ⇒ A: A's non-unit productions are aA | a  →  add C → aA | a
then delete the unit productions themselves

steps.title: Step 4 · Useless symbols again
steps.explain: Steps 2 and 3 can orphan symbols: deleting a unit production may remove the only arrow into a variable. So run 1a and 1b once more on the current grammar.
lines: generating, round 1: S (S → b)   A (A → a)   B (B → b)   C (C → a)
generating, round 2: nothing new → stop
not generating: none, so all 4 variables survive
reachable, round 0: S
reachable, round 1: S → AB reaches A, B   S → b reaches b   S → bC reaches C
reachable, round 2: A → aA reaches a
unreachable from S: none

steps.title: Check: same language, smaller grammar
steps.explain: Finish by writing the final grammar in full, naming the three properties it now has, and checking the language on short strings. It catches the commonest slip: dropping a production that was doing real work.
lines: before: S → AB | b   A → aA | ε   B → bC | b   C → A
after:  S → AB | b | bC   A → aA | a   B → bC | b   C → aA | a
no useless symbols ✓ · no ε-productions ✓ · no unit productions ✓
productions: 7 → 9   ·   variables: 4 → 4
L unchanged: compared on every string of length ≤ 10 (55 strings of the language) ✓
